items.title: Prohibited Jurisdictions
items.description: Although the registered domain appears to implement geo-blocking, the prohibited jurisdictions list available in the T&Cs does not include Curacao or the Netherlands. Players residing in Curacao, the Netherlands (and any country forming part of the kingdom of the Netherlands), USA, UN sanctioned countries and FATF blacklisted countries must not be allowed to register. Kindly amend.

items.title: ID verification procedure
items.description: ID verification procedure

items.title: Account closure procedure
items.description: Account closure procedure upon the operator becoming aware that the player is a minor post-registration.

items.title: Record-keeping
items.description: Record-keeping

items.title: Contacting the operator
items.description: Procedure on how the player can contact the operator regarding RG concerns via email or chat

items.title: Language
items.description: Must be available in English and target market language

items.title: Vulnerable gamblers
items.description: RG policy should include a structured process on flagging potential vulnerable gamblers

items.title: Indicators of problem gambling
items.description: Must have a structured process for responding to indicators of problem gambling

items.title: Player profiling and Risk Assessment
items.description: Establish player profiles to assess risk levels

items.title: Monitoring and intervention
items.description: Adopt RBA to determine level of monitoring and intervention

items.title: Recording RG interactions
items.description: Record all RG interactions in PAM system

items.title: Identification of vulnerable persons
items.description: Procedure to follow for players identified as vulnerable persons

items.title: Cooling-off period
items.description: Operator must offer players option to activate a cooling-off period

items.title: Cooling-off options
items.description: Options for cooling-off must include duration and marketing opt-out at minimum

items.title: Self-Exclusion
items.description: Operator must offer players the option to self-exclude themselves for a duration of at least 1 year

items.title: Deposit Limits
items.description: Players must be able to set limits on the total amount they deposit

items.title: Training and Staff Readiness
items.description: Operators must train customer service and Responsible Gaming staff to handle player interaction profesionally and effectively

items.title: Consumer Advertising and Marketing
items.description: Operators must not engage in irresponsible advertising

items.title: Internet Filtering Tools
items.description: The operator is advised to remind adults that they should take precautions when sharing devices with minors

items.title: Notifications for concerning behaviours
items.description: Operators may employ automatic or manual pop-up notifications in response to concerning behaviours

items.title: Initiating direct contact
items.description: When a player exhibits behaviour that reasonably suggests they may be a Vulnerable Player, the operator must initiate direct contact

items.title: Other Limits
items.description: Other limits may be considered including loss limits, time limits or wager limits, in line wth the operator's target player and/or market

items.title: Lodging a complaint
items.description: The policy must state that players may lodge a complaint free of charge at any time up to six months of the settlement of the bet or the incident about which they are making a complaint.

items.title: Lodging a complaint (P2P)
items.description: The policy must state that in the case of P2P (such as poker) or ante post fixed odds betting the six month clock begins after the bet settlement or conclusion of a specific event rather than the placement of the wager after the bet settlement or conclusion of a specific event rather than the placement of the wager.

items.title: Lodging a complaint (live betting)
items.description: The policy must state that in the case of complaints about in-running sports betting, customers must be advised that while they may submit a complaint within six months, prompt action may be necessary if the investigation may depend on data specific to the complaint which — due to the nature of in-running betting.

items.title: Eligibility to make a complaint
items.description: The complaints procedure must state that complaints can only be made by the registered player.

items.title: Complaint form
items.description: An official Complaint Submission Form must be available to the player. a. This form must be either a downloadable form that can be completed and emailed or otherwise uploaded by the player, and/or a form that is fully completed and submitted online b. The form must include at a minimum the following sections i. Complainant's name, address, and place of residence. ii. Complainant's account number (if applicable) iii. Date of the complaint and date of the disputed event. iv. Description of the conduct being disputed (using a selection of predetermined category topics if/as applicable). c. The form must be available in English and in the language of the website/domain that the player is using. d. The operator may request supporting documentation the player requires to include as part of the complaint. Any additional information or documentation requested by the operator must be a reasonable in the context of complaint resolution.

items.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution
items.description: The operator must offer an ADR option for the players, subject to the requirements of Clause 5 of the Player Complaints Policy Guidelines.

items.title: Legal action restrictions
items.description: Except if mutually agreed under specific terms of ADR (Clause 5 of the Player Complaints Policy Guideline), the operator must not restrict the rights of the player him/herself to take legal action.

items.title: Prioritising RG-related complaints
items.description: Complaints related to responsible gaming should be prioritized due to potential impacts on player well-being. Complaints should be categorized as related to responsible gaming in any case when it regards targeting of Vulnerable Players, the availability and/or timely implementation of self-exclusion and/or cooling-off and the mandated consequences therein as outlined in the Responsible Gaming policy.

items.title: Timeline for RG-related complaints
items.description: Operators must use best in efforts to resolve these cases within five business days.

items.title: RG-related complaints process
items.description: The policy must state that within two days of receiving a complaint, the operator will: - Confirm receipt of the complaint in writing. - Provide an explanation of how the complaint will be processed. - Provide notice of the average timeline for resolution of such complaints.

items.title: Extension of timeline for RG-related complaints
items.description: If more time is needed by the operator to make a reasonable and informed decision, players must be informed of the delay, which cannot exceed two weeks. If a delay is due to a lack of or a slow response from the player, the resolution period may be extended by no more than a further two weeks.

items.title: Timeline for all other complaint types
items.description: The operator will assess and respond to complaints within four weeks. If necessary, due to complexity or lack of information, this period may be extended once by an additional four weeks, with prior written notice to the player.

items.title: Process for all other complaint types
items.description: The policy must state that within one week of receiving a complaint, the operator will: - Confirm receipt of the complaint in writing. - Provide an explanation of how the complaint will be processed. - Provide notice of the average timeline for resolution of such complaints.

items.title: Final determination letter
items.description: A player will always receive a final determination of their complaint in writing. The response will either be: 1. A reasoned final assessment of the outcome/resolution of the complaint with supporting evidence if necessary or applicable. 2. Detailed reasons for not handling the complaint. If additional information is reasonably required to address the complaint fully, the operator must have requested this information within the initial four week time period. Should the complainant not provide the necessary within the initial four week time period, the operator may reject the complaint. 3. If the player is unsatisfied with the resolution and makes a further complaint to that effect, the player is informed that they may escalate the matter to an independent ADR entity.

items.title: Escalation to ADR
items.description: If a complaint cannot be resolved internally, the operator must provide players with an independent ADR service, of which the operator will bear all costs.

items.title: Recommencing ADR process with a different entity
items.description: The policy must state that once the ADR process is completed it cannot be recommenced by either the player or the operator with another different ADR entity.

items.title: Recommencing dropped ADR processes
items.description: The policy must state that in the event that the player drops out of the ADR process (but it has already begun) the player should not have the right to resurface the dispute in the future.

items.title: Restrictions on ADR escalation
items.description: Provision of ADR services by the operator is mandatory. If the operator sets ADR parameters in order to prevent abuse (such as whether ADR must be undertaken before a player can initiate legal proceedings, the binding nature of the ADR outcome on the player, or whether there is a minimum claim value required for escalation to ADR), the CGA advises the operator to carefully consider these conditions and seek independent legal advice regarding any applicable civil legislation.

items.title: Periodic reporting
items.description: The policy must state that the operator will submit reports to the CGA on January 15th and June 15th based on complaints submitted to the operator since the previous reporting period by players using the Complaints Submission Form.

items.title: Report details
items.description: The policy must state that the periodic report will summarise the following: a. Total number of complaints made b. Total number of settled complaints (upheld and rejected) c. Number of pending or unresolved complaints d. Number of complaints by category e. Number referred to ADR f. Number and detail of complaints for which a player has taken legal action

items.title: Record-Keeping of unresolved complaints
items.description: The policy must state that the operator will ensure that records of unresolved complaints and/or complaints that have been escalated to ADR or legal proceedings will be kept for the lesser of five years or the relevant time stipulated by data protection, statute of limitations or other relevant laws or guidelines.

items.title: CGA's right to access records
items.description: The policy must state that in light of the fact that the CGA reserves the right to request, at any time, access to records of complaints received as well as any disputes that are pending resolution, the operator shall ensure that such records are readily available at all times.

items.title: Right to make a complaint
items.description: The policy must state that the player has the right to make a complaint regarding any part of their relationship with the operator, or any incident related to their participation in a game of chance. This includes (but is not limited to): 1. Deposit issues 2. Withdrawal issues 3. Bonus terms and conditions 4. Account closures or restrictions 5. Alleged errors or unfairness in game outcomes 6. Responsible gaming issues 7. Treatment of player balances 8. KYC and Verification 9. Data Protection 10. Technical or Software issues 11. AML concerns 12. Issues with minors 13. Fraudulent games 14. Fraudulent practices 15. License or regulation 16. Unfair terms and conditions
